archive.question: Why do LLMs still struggle with financial questions even when they have access to SEC filings? Is the bigger problem finding the right information or reasoning about it?

support.quote: Enterprise Comparison QA (EC-QA) evaluates the model’s ability to align disclosures from different companies and identify salient differences across structured metrics and narrative content, despite variations in reporting style. Longitudinal Tracking QA (LT-QA) examines whether the model can detect trends and shifts across filings from the same company over time, including structural or semantic changes under evolving disclosure frames.

We benchmark 17 leading LLMs, spanning open-source, closed-source, and finance-specialized models, under both ground-truth context and retrieval-augmented settings. Results show substantial performance degradation, with accuracy dropping by 18.60% and 14.35% as tasks shift from single-document reasoning to longitudinal and cross-entity analysis. This degradation is associated with increased comparison hallucinations, temporal and entity mismatches, and is further reflected in declines in reasoning quality and factual consistency—limitations that existing benchmarks have yet to formally categorize or quantify.

claim.text: Access to filings does not ensure that a model connects evidence correctly: it must align companies, reporting periods, and disclosures whose wording or structure changes. Across 17 evaluated LLMs, the paper reports accuracy drops of 18.60% for longitudinal analysis and 14.35% for cross-company analysis relative to single-document reasoning, associated with hallucinated comparisons and confusion about times and entities.
